Title: Voter support alone not enough to form government, says Amirudin
Article:
KLANG: Increased voter support alone is insufficient to form a government, with cooperation between political coalitions proving to be a decisive factor, says Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
The Pakatan Harapan (PH) election director said forming a government required more than just election strategies, as political parties also needed to reach an understanding and work together with other coalitions.
He said preliminary results of the Melaka state election showed positive gains in support, particularly among Malay voters and younger people.
However, he said the gains were not enough to secure a stronger position for PH.
"There were some fairly positive increases for certain parties, particularly in Malay votes, which we can discuss.
"But it is not enough because the issue is not just about coalitions or support for a coalition, but how political alignments should be considered to form a government.
"In the end, the formula for success in Malaysia is through a successful coalition. Today, coalitions are no longer just between political parties, but between coalitions themselves. This is something our leaders must consider carefully," he said.
He was responding to questions on changes in support for PH following the Melaka election.
Amirudin, who is also Selangor menteri besar, was speaking after officiating the 2026 National PIBKS Digital Education Carnival here today.
Asked whether PH needed to change its political strategy, he said support for the coalition remained intact and had increased in several areas.
However, he said he had yet to obtain the detailed Melaka election results to conduct a comprehensive assessment of PH's performance.
In the 16th Melaka state election yesterday, BN and Perikatan Nasional (PN) won a combined 24 of the 28 state seats, securing more than a two-thirds majority in the state assembly.
According to official Election Commission results, BN won 21 seats, PN secured three, while PH won four.

Title: Heavy rain floods homes in 2 Penang villages
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Heavy rain flooded homes and access roads in two Penang villages today, as water levels rose rapidly in low-lying areas.
The affected areas were Kampung Tasik Junjung in Simpang Ampat and Kampung Sulup in Teluk Kumbar.
No evacuations had been reported.
TikTok live broadcasts showed residents in Simpang Ampat moving their belongings to higher ground.
Floodwaters also entered several homes in Kampung Sulup, Teluk Kumbar.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department had earlier issued a thunderstorm and heavy rain warning for several states, including Penang, during the ongoing northeast monsoon transition. Rain continued in several parts of the state.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No pressure on Anwar to dissolve Parliament, says Dzulkefly
Article:
SEREMBAN: There is currently no pressure on Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to dissolve Parliament to pave the way for the 16th general election (GE16), says Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah) vice-president Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad.
He said the prime minister had his own considerations on the appropriate time to dissolve Parliament, adding that the Federal Government's current term had yet to expire and Anwar continued to enjoy majority support among members of parliament.
"I think we should wait. There is no pressure to make any sudden move to dissolve Parliament.
"We should wait until the end of the term, unless something drastic happens. We should prioritise the positive economic momentum that the people are enjoying today," he told reporters after officiating the 2026 National Wanita Muda Amanah Convention (Warda) at Klana Resort here today.
Dzulkefly, who is also health minister, was commenting on calls for Parliament to be dissolved following the Melaka election, in which BN and PN secured a combined 24 seats while Pakatan Harapan (PH) won four.
He said the people should first be given the opportunity to enjoy the benefits of the Unity Government's efforts, citing positive economic indicators, foreign investments and rising household incomes.
He also said Malaysia's economic performance had received recognition from international analytical bodies, claiming the country ranked among the world's 15 best-performing economies after climbing 19 places.
Dzulkefly said any move that could undermine political and economic stability or national harmony was undesirable, adding that the people's well-being should remain the priority.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Jordan sentences three men to death over deadly church attack
Article:
AMMAN:  Jordan's State Security Court sentenced three men to death on Sunday for carrying out an attack on a church in the southern governorate of Karak last month that killed nine people, the state news agency Petra reported.
The court convicted the men of offences including carrying out terrorist acts resulting in death, possessing weapons and ammunition for terrorist purposes and promoting the ideology of a terrorist group. The ruling is subject to appeal and automatic review by the Court of Cassation, Petra said.
Gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hamoud on October 23, in a rare attack on Jordan's Christian minority. Authorities said 34 people were also wounded.
Security forces arrested the three men on October 26 after a shootout at an abandoned house in Karak. All three were wounded, while no security personnel were injured, according to the Public Security Directorate.
Jordan, a US partner in the fight against extremism, later that day launched airstrikeson southern Syria against groups it linked to the church attack. Syrian authorities said seven people, including three children and a woman, were killed.
Jordan later acknowledged that its airstrikes had killed civilians in Syria and the two countries agreed to form a joint security committee to review the incident and its consequences. — REUTERS

Title: Health Ministry targets full capacity at Pasir Gudang Hospital
Article:
SEREMBAN: The Health Ministry will prioritise efforts to bring Pasir Gudang Hospital in Johor to full operational capacity, from its current level of 85 per cent.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the ministry was implementing an aggressive plan to fill vacant positions to ensure the hospital could operate at full capacity, with 304 beds and 16 delivery rooms.
He said the placement of nurses and medical specialists at the hospital was currently based on its operational capacity.
"Our current operational level is 85 per cent. I have already answered this matter in Parliament. We have not been able to fill all the positions for doctors and specialists.
"However, the current placement of specialists and doctors allows us to operate at 85 per cent. Many departments have already begun operating," he told reporters after officiating the Amanah National Young Women's Convention 2026.
Earlier, the media reported that Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi had raised concerns over the hospital's operational needs.
Of the 2,271 positions allocated to the hospital, only 1,276 had been filled as of Nov 6.
Dzulkefly said the ministry remained committed to meeting Johor's healthcare needs.
Located in Bandar Seri Alam, Pasir Gudang, the hospital began operations in stages on Aug 1, 2025.
Its construction cost RM375.5 million and was aimed at improving access to healthcare for residents of Pasir Gudang and surrounding areas, while helping to ease congestion at Sultanah Aminah Hospital and Sultan Ismail Hospital.

Title: 40-year-old structure caused Kuala Kangsar water tank burst
Article:
IPOH: The bursting of a 455-cubic-metre water tank at Taman Kuala Kangsar yesterday was caused by the deterioration of its structure, which was more than 40 years old.
Perak Infrastructure, Energy, Water and Public Transport Committee chairman Datuk Seri Mohammad Nizar Jamaluddin said the Perak Water Board's (LAP) Kuala Kangsar operations centre received information about the incident about 5pm.
The incident affected water supply to about 520 consumers in the surrounding areas.
He said LAP had carried out cleaning works on roads around the damaged tank, while direct water supply through the main pipeline had been provided to the affected areas of Taman Kuala Kangsar and Taman Meranti.
"The removal of all affected tank panels has been carried out, and plans are being made to replace the tank with a new one.
"In addition, LAP is conducting a comprehensive technical assessment of the old tank structure before installation of the new tank begins," he said in a statement today.
Nizar said preliminary investigations at the scene found that water from the burst tank had overflowed onto surrounding roads, but no casualties or property damage had been reported.
"An inspection of the house nearest to the tank also found that it was safe and had sustained no damage," he said.
He said water supply to the affected areas remained stable and uninterrupted, while LAP's Kuala Kangsar operations centre would continue monitoring the situation to prevent further disruptions and ensure the incident did not recur.
Several videos of the incident have gone viral on social media since yesterday, causing panic among residents.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Megaspeed says Alice Huang left company in August 2025
Article:
SINGAPORE: Megaspeed said on Sunday that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, whose ties to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang raised US national security concerns, had officially left Megaspeed on Aug 30, 2025, and had no current role at the Singapore-based company.
"Megaspeed does not comment on Ms. Huang's personal and private matters," the company added in a statement.
"Megaspeed is aware of recent media reports containing assertions about our business, supply chain and global operations that are not supported by verifiable evidence."
The company said it conducted "legitimate and lawful business" and had retained external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation.
On Friday, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that four government agencies favoured putting Megaspeed, the Singapore company at the heart of the Nvidia scandal, on a trade black list but not the Commerce Department that was in charge.
Bessent said Treasury, Pentagon, the State Department and the US Trade Representative's Office had favoured adding Megaspeed to the Commerce Department entity list for months.
"But Commerce has the pen," Bessent told CNBC's "Squawk Box." "You will have to ask them about their internal processes."
The Commerce Department's so-called entity list is a trade blacklist of groups connected to China that US officials say pose national security risks.
The department did not immediately return a request for comment.
There is growing criticism of Secretary of Commerce, Howard Lutnick's role in overseeing export controls on US chips to China.
Lutnick reportedly stalled President Donald Trump's crackdown on companies suspected of diverting Nvidia's ‌chips to China, media outlets reported this week.
Republican Senator John Curtis said that "Secretary Lutnick's reported stalling on export controls raises the question of whether the Commerce Department is acting in the best interests of the American people."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN plans to field PPP candidates in next general election
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional plans to field People's Progressive Party candidates in the next general election, subject to agreement from MIC's top leadership.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the plan would require the agreement of MIC president Tan Sri SA Vigneswaran and deputy president Datuk Seri M Saravanan.
"I am determined that, with the agreement of Tan Sri Viki (Vigneswaran) and Datuk Seri Saravanan, we will field PPP candidates in the next general election," he said at the PPP Deepavali open house here today.
In January, PPP, previously known as MyPPP, was readmitted as a component party of the coalition.
Zahid said he respected PPP president Datuk Dr Loga Bala Mohan for keeping the party in BN.
He also referred to BN's recent election victories in Johor, Negri Sembilan and Melaka, saying that despite differences of opinion, the coalition had come together again as one family.
"In a football tournament, three wins in a row is a hat-trick. This is a very stylish victory for BN.
"This is a people's movement. It is also divine intervention," he said.
He said BN had to work hard and smart but, most importantly, show care and courtesy to all Malaysians, regardless of religion, race, ethnicity or language.
"We do not need to shout and scream or keep saying 'sakau' here and there.
"We talk about the good things. Let people say what they want about us, but we will speak well of ourselves. This is the beauty of BN," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nearly 1,500 migrants arrive in Canary Islands in one day
Article:
MADRID: Almost 1,500 migrants arrived in Spain's Canary Islands on Saturday, the highest number in a single day since 2020, the EFE news agency reported on Sunday, citing the maritime rescue service.
A total of 1,488 people in 14 boats were rescued by the Spanish coastguard, EFE reported, continuing a surge of arrivals from West African countries to the Spanish archipelago since October.
The previous one-day record was the 1,461 people rescued in waters off the Canary Islands on Nov 7, 2020, maritime rescue services said on Sunday.
While migrant arrivals have declined so far this year compared with the same period last year, the sharp increase last month placed additional pressure on reception and emergency services on some of the Canary Islands, particularly the smaller and less densely populated ones.
One boat on Saturday was carrying 240 people, including 12 women and 36 children, authorities said. The rescued migrants were taken to El Hierro, one of the smallest Canary Islands.
Most of the people were from Senegal, Gambia and Guinea Conakry.
Twelve boats arrived in El Hierro, plus one in Gran Canaria and another in Tenerife.
Spain's Territorial Policy Minister Angel Victor Torres will visit El Hierro on Sunday to discuss the surge in migrant arrivals.
The Atlantic route from West Africa to the Canary Islands is one of the world's deadliest migration crossings.
Thousands of migrants attempt the journey each year in overcrowded boats, seeking to reach Spanish territory despite rough seas, strong currents and long distances.
Arrivals tend to pick up in the autumn months, when sea conditions along the route are generally calmer and more favourable for crossings.
Migrant arrivals to the Canary Islands between January and Oct 31 were down 5.5 per cent from the same period last year, government data show.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia was frank on steps taken over forest fires, Asean chair says
Article:
MANILA: The Philippines' foreign minister said on Sunday that Indonesia was very candid in expressing what it had done to address forest fires.
"The leaders also encouraged the Asean member states to prioritise the ratification of the Asean Coordinating Center on Transboundary Haze Pollution Control," Foreign Minister Theresa Lazaro told a news briefing.
On Friday, a study said thousands of hectares of land on palm oil and pulpwood concessions run by large listed firms were burnt during Indonesia's worst fire season in years, highlighting the role of deforestation and land clearing.
Indonesia's forest fires caused a spike in respiratory illness at home and triggered air pollution warnings and school closures across the region, with fire emissions surging to three times the seasonal average.
A total of 2.88 million hectares of land were damaged by fire from January to October this year, driven by intense El Nino weather conditions and extreme heat, as well as clearing of forests to make way for industrial-scale palm oil and pulpwood plantations, according to a joint study by Rainforest Action Network (RAN) and geomonitoring platform Nusantara Atlas.
Another report quoting scientists said, wildfires that hit large parts of Indonesia from August to October and plunged much of Southeast Asia into hazardous smoke were made much worse by "record-breaking" heat caused by human-induced climate change.
While a very strong El Nino was the dominant factor in determining the extremely low levels of rainfall across Indonesia from July, human-induced climate change contributed around 1.6 degrees Celsius of additional heat during the fire season, said a report by climate research group World Weather Attribution.
"The conditions that we saw this year would simply just not have happened in a world without the human contribution to climate change, even with the very strong El Nino that we're seeing," said Theodore Keeping, a researcher into wildfires and extreme weather at Imperial College London who contributed to the report.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 1,606 flood victims remain at relief centres in 3 states
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 1,606 flood victims from 432 families remained at nine temporary relief centres in Selangor, Perak and Sarawak as of 4.30pm.
The Social Welfare Department's Info Bencana portal recorded the highest number of evacuees in Selangor, with 1,408 people from 373 families housed at seven centres in Kuala Selangor.
In Perak, 191 people from 58 families were staying at two centres in Hilir Perak.
In Sarawak, seven people from one family remained at a relief centre in Miri.
Of the total evacuees, 497 were adult women, 475 adult men, 270 girls, 316 boys, 32 baby boys and 16 baby girls.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Buried under hot tar, 11-year-old Hasya Fahira needs surgery
Article:
BATU PAHAT: An 11-year-old girl who lost both parents when a tar-laden lorry crushed their multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) in Parit Yaani will undergo plastic surgery for injuries to her left thigh.
Johor Islamic Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Khalid said specialists from Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) would be brought to Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital (HSNI) to perform the procedure, sparing the girl, Hasya Fahira Zulkifli, from having to be transferred.
He said her injuries were more severe than those sustained by her younger brother, Muhammad Adam Mohd Hardi, 8, after both children were buried under hot tar in the Nov 1 accident.
"The Johor Islamic Religious Council (MAIJ) will cover all costs involved, including any additional expenses," he said after accompanying Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi on a visit to the siblings at HSNI today.
Onn Hafiz also celebrated Hasya Fahira's birthday, which falls today.
Fared said arrangements were also being made for both children to receive survivors' pensions from the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso), as their late father had previously worked and contributed to the scheme.
Pending approval, MAIJ would provide monthly living assistance to their uncle, who is caring for the siblings.
He said the state government was also prepared to cover any additional expenses arising from the children's needs.
In the 12.30pm accident, the children's parents, Tengku Syafirana Tengku Abdullah, 44, and Mohd Hardi Mohd Husin, 46,
were killed
when a tar-laden lorry overturned and crushed their MPV along Jalan Yong Peng-Muar near Parit Yaani.
The lorry had reportedly suffered a burst tyre.
Hardi sustained head and arm injuries, as well as burns to several parts of his body, while his wife suffered severe head and internal injuries, as well as burns.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Urgent climate finance pleas at COP31 face a non-urgent response
Article:
URGENT pleas for cash from poor nations most exposed to the kind of climate-related disasters that have marked this year risk meeting a sluggish response at Turkiye's COP31 talks as Western governments put national security and living costs first.
Two years ago, rich countries agreed at UN climate talks they would triple climate funding for poorer countries to US$300 billion per year by 2035 versus a previous 2020 target.
Also by 2035, financing from all public and private sources combined would be US$1.3 trillion annually.
The rich countries met their 2020 target two years late.
Since then, climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as US President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and the Middle East have added to inflationary pressures and the need to spend on security.
Vulnerable small island nations say the cash they need to repair damage and to guard against future climate-related crises is again arriving too slowly and their own budgets have shrunk.
"Like many small island developing states, we remain in a perpetual climate disaster recovery mode," Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale told the conference. "We cannot build resilience while our fiscal space erodes."
Even when money is available, technical hurdles set by lenders can stretch the administrative capacity of small states.
For many developed nations, facing international and domestic unrest as citizens protest against the rising cost of living, their focus has narrowed.
Britain, which has sought to be a leader in addressing climate change, said in July savings made from switching some climate finance contributions from grants to loans would be used to help fund a cap on domestic bus fares.
Meanwhile, defence spending has climbed significantly.
The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute estimated in April that world military expenditure reached US$2.89 trillion in 2025, up 2.9 per cent in real terms from 2024.
Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine said military defence ultimately was the smaller concern.
"We are told there is no money, but as spending on war grows, the greatest security threat we face remains underfunded. I appeal to you: Find money for life, not death," she said in her speech to the conference in the Turkish Mediterranean city of Antalya on Wednesday.
COP31 SEEKING IMPLEMENTATION, NOT NEW TARGETS
As they respond to the contemporary mood, host country Turkey and lead negotiator Australia have emphasised making previous pledges work, rather than securing a new headline target at the conference, which continues until the end of next week.
"COP31 must respond to the global moment and send a clear message to accelerate implementation," Australia's COP31 negotiating president Chris Bowen said. He also said finance must be "faster, simpler and fairer."
[[nid:1578415]]
Analysis by previous COP host Brazil published earlier this week found that US$137 billion was mobilised in 2024, a slight increase on 2023, but that direct aid and future commitments to multilateral funds were lower.
Current trends suggested provision would fall US$840 billion short of the US$1.3 trillion goal, it said.
"Geopolitical tensions, constrained fiscal space in many developing countries and the high cost of capital where it is most needed are among the obstacles," the report said.
By way of solutions, it urged measures such as risk-sharing and clearer links between national plans and budgets.
Some smaller nations have taken novel steps to find cash and to spur richer nations to match it.
The Solomon Islands pledged US$400,000 from its own pocket on Thursday, saying it was determined to show leadership and calling on rich countries to do the same.
The Bahamas committed US$75 million to protect and restore its seagrass meadows, which store carbon, to try to persuade investors to fund verified carbon projects.
UNCLOGGING THE SYSTEM TO GET MONEY FLOWING
Both public and private funding provide climate finance grants, loans, aid and investment in measures ranging from renewable energy to flood defences.
Multilateral development banks are a conduit for finance that leverages capital provided by shareholder countries to increase lending power and they say they are delivering.
Their lending reached record levels in 2025, according to the European Investment Bank.
But, they could do more, according to Washington-based think tank the Center for Global Development and recipients of the finance have said the development banks should make access easier.
Addressing that, a group of multilateral funds told the COP31 talks they would rely more on one another's assessments in co-financed operations rather than having to go through multiple overlapping processes.
For private investors, the most obvious issue is the risk of investing in an instrument that does not guarantee returns.
Given how unforthcoming the world's richer governments have been, the private sector is ever more important.
"Our clients see opportunities in the energy transition, but they need reliable power, predictable costs and confidence in customer demand before they invest," HSBC Chief Sustainability Officer Julian Wentzel said.
"COP31 needs to help create that confidence."
* The writers are from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Selangor prioritises three areas for flood mitigation
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Selangor has identified Kampung Melayu Subang, Kampung Kubu Gajah and Puncak Alam as priority areas for flood mitigation works.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the three areas experienced more serious flooding, particularly during the early stages of the Northeast Monsoon and monsoon transition periods.
The state has allocated RM36.45 million for 47 flood mitigation projects under its 2027 Budget.
He said the state government would review the locations earmarked for the projects based on current needs and ensure efforts to reduce flood risks continued.
"We will review them because this is an ongoing effort, and the three main areas are Kampung Melayu Subang, Kampung Kubu Gajah and Puncak Alam.
"These are three areas that experience serious flooding during the early stages of the monsoon or during the monsoon transition," he told reporters after officiating an education carnival.
Also present were Education Ministry Daily School Management Division director Mohd Hanafi Samad and Selangor Education Department director Datin Wan Nor Ashikin Abu Kassim.
Amirudin said Kuala Selangor also faced flooding, but problems in some areas, such as Parit Mahang, involved stagnant flooding and required specific attention as a longer-term issue.
He said the state government would seek to implement the projects as soon as possible and assess the effectiveness of flood mitigation measures in areas that had frequently been affected.
He said conditions had improved in several areas, including Dengkil and Kuala Langat, following mitigation efforts.
"These efforts will focus on 56 identified flood hotspots.
"Between 2016 and 2017, we had nearly 200 flood hotspots, but the number has since declined through the measures implemented, with several areas successfully addressed," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Green Data Centre Certification needed to ensure sustainable growth, says Lam Thye
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government should consider introducing mandatory Green Data Centre Certification to ensure that operators comply with measurable environmental performance standards, said Alliance for a Safe Community chairman Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye.
He said the rapid expansion of data centres in Malaysia, driven by growing demand for artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing and digital technology, must not come at the expense of environmental sustainability.
"Malaysia must strike the right balance between technological advancement, economic growth and environmental protection," he said in a statement today.
Lee called for stringent environmental requirements for major data centre developments, including assessments of their cumulative impact on electricity and water resources, as well as the surrounding environment.
He also proposed mandatory sustainability standards covering energy efficiency, water consumption and carbon emissions, supported by regular independent audits.
He said data centre operators should progressively increase their use of renewable energy and adopt more energy-efficient cooling technologies to reduce pressure on the national electricity grid.
On water security, he expressed concern that the substantial volume of water required for cooling operations could affect local communities, particularly in areas already facing water supply challenges.
He urged operators to prioritise recycled and reclaimed water, rainwater harvesting and water-efficient cooling technologies rather than relying excessively on treated drinking water.
"The construction of large data centre facilities may involve extensive land clearing, potentially affecting green spaces, biodiversity, natural habitats and local drainage systems," he said.
In addition, he called for greater accountability in managing electronic waste generated through the replacement of servers, batteries and other equipment.
To improve transparency, Lee said data centre operators should be required to disclose their electricity and water consumption, carbon emissions and overall environmental performance.
He said the government should review investment incentives and approval conditions to ensure that companies receiving government incentives demonstrate genuine commitments to sustainable development.
He said data centre development must be planned according to the availability of electricity, water and supporting infrastructure to avoid placing additional burdens on public utilities and local communities.
"Digital transformation must not become an environmental burden. Economic progress must not compromise our water security, energy sustainability and quality of life," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NMR152 rice variety offers hope of higher padi yields for Kedah farmers
Article:
ALOR STAR: Farmers participating in the Kedah Zakat Board's (LZNK) Asnaf Large-Scale Smart Padi Field (SBBA) project could potentially increase their yields to 11 tonnes per hectare using a new nuclear technology-based rice variety, NMR152.
Malaysian Nuclear Agency research officer Dr Sobri Hussein said the variety was developed through nuclear-based mutation breeding, with the potential for higher yields, greater weather resilience and improved agronomic traits.
However, he said that good farm management remained crucial, as the variety alone could contribute only about 50 per cent towards higher yields, with the remainder depending on farming practices.
"As such, farmers must pay attention to fertilisation, disease control and soil conditions to achieve good yields. We hope this variety, which took 10 years to develop, will bring better returns to farmers," he said after a handover of NMR152 seeds from Malaysian Nuclear Agency director-general Dr Muhammad Rawi Mohamed Zin to LZNK chief executive officer Datuk Syeikh Zakaria Othman.
The pilot project involves the distribution of 2,000kg of certified NMR152 seeds, packed in 100 bags, to LZNK at Kampung Alor Melintang, to strengthen the rice farming ecosystem under the waqf agriculture concept.
Sobri said research had found the variety suitable for areas prone to drought and those with less favourable soil conditions.
He cited areas with rocky and sandy soil, where farmers had previously struggled to achieve good yields but recorded improvements after using NMR152.
He also assured the public that the variety was safe for cultivation and consumption.
Meanwhile, SBBA participant representative Iza Faizal Halim, 50, said the new variety offered hope to about 10 project participants of regaining their previous highest yields.
"Previously, we used the 297 variety, which produced about six to seven tonnes per hectare. We hope NMR152 will help us achieve more than 10 tonnes per hectare, similar to the yields we recorded about two years ago," he said.
Rawi said the collaboration with LZNK was aimed at helping farmers increase their yields and income through the use of NMR152 seeds.
He said the pilot project would assess the variety's effectiveness in improving crop productivity and rice production, while creating opportunities to boost farmers' income.
Syeikh Zakaria said LZNK was committed to identifying the best rice varieties and would seek advice from Malaysian Nuclear Agency on expanding the use of NMR152 across its projects if the trial proved successful.
He added that LZNK remained open to collaboration with various agencies to improve yields, reduce production costs and share farming practices that could benefit farmers throughout Kedah.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid: BN will not contest Sarawak election
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional (BN) has confirmed that it will not contest the 13th Sarawak election next month.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the decision was in line with an understanding between Umno and Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB).
"BN has no intention of contesting any state seats in Sarawak, as this is the understanding between Umno and PBB in Sarawak.
"Umno and BN have never intended to field any candidates in the Sarawak election," he told reporters after attending the People's Progressive Party's Deepavali open house here today.
The 13th Sarawak election will be held on Dec 12, with nomination day on Nov 28 and early voting on Dec 8.
Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) chairman and Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Abang Openg
will announce the coalition's 82 candidates
for the election on Nov 25.
Abang Johari said the list would comprise candidates from all four component parties.
GPS comprises PBB, Sarawak United People's Party (SUPP), Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS) and Progressive Democratic Party (PDP).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: GOF seizes 50,000 sticks of untaxed cigarettes worth RM125,000 in Pasir Puteh
Article:
KOTA BARU: The General Operations Force (GOF) seized 50,000 sticks of cigarettes suspected to be untaxed with a value of RM93,500, during a raid on a house in Kampung Gong Serapat, Pasir Puteh, last night.
A 36-year-old Pakistani national was also arrested during the operation, which took place about 8pm on Nov 14 as part of Op Taring Wawasan Kelantan.
GOF Southeast Brigade commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain said today that the total value of the seizure is estimated at RM125,000.
This includes a grey Nissan Grand Livina valued at RM30,000 and a mobile phone worth RM1,500.
He said the cigarettes were discovered inside several sacks in the rear of the vehicle at the scene.
"The operation was carried out by a team from the Strike Force of Company A, 7th Battalion of the GOF (based in Kuantan, Pahang), with assistance from the battalion's intelligence unit," he said.
He said the suspect had been living in Malaysia for nearly 13 years, was married to a Malaysian woman and had four children.
Radzi said the suspect is believed to have obtained the untaxed cigarettes from an unidentified local man in the vicinity of Melor, Kota Baru, through an intermediary known as 'Ubai', with orders placed based on demand.
He added that the suspect and all seized items have been handed over to the Criminal Investigation Division of the Pasir Puteh district police headquarters.
The case is being investigated under Section 135(1)(d) of the Customs Act 1967.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid congratulates Rauf on his appointment as Melaka CM
Article:
MELAKA: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has congratulated Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh on his appointment as the chief minister of Melaka for a second term.
The Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman said the trust placed in him by the people carries a significant responsibility to continue the efforts already established, strengthen the state's stability, and ensure that all development initiatives truly benefit the people of Melaka.
"God willing, I am confident that, given his experience and leadership, the progress of Melaka will continue, and more opportunities will be created for the people throughout the state.
"May Allah SWT grant wisdom and guidance to YAB Datuk Seri Utama as he shoulders this trust, and may he continue to lead Melaka toward a more advanced and prosperous future," he said in a Facebook post today.
Earlier, Rauf, 65,
took his oath of office as the chief minister of Mela
ka before the Yang Dipertua Negeri, Tun Mohd Ali Mohd Rustam, at the Main Hall of the Office of the Yang Dipertua Negeri on Jalan Seri Negeri, Ayer Keroh.
In the 16th Melaka state election, which concluded yesterday, Rauf successfully defended his Tanjung Bidara state seat, defeating Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate Yunazri Mustamiri by a majority of 8,615 votes in a straight fight.
The BN–Perikatan Nasional (PN) coalition
secured a more than two-thirds
majority to form the state government, with BN winning 21 seats and PN securing three out of the 28 contested state legislative assembly seats.
Pakatan Harapan (PH) won four seats. — BERNAMA

Title: Palestine marks 38th anniversary of statehood declaration
Article:
RAMALLAH: Today marks the 38th anniversary of the declaration of the State of Palestine, proclaimed by late Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat in Algiers on Nov 15, 1988, Palestine News and Info Agency (WAFA) reported.
"In the name of God and in the name of the Palestinian Arab people, the National Council declares the creation of the State of Palestine on our Palestinian land, with noble Jerusalem as its capital," Arafat announced during a meeting of the Palestinian National Council (PNC), the Palestine Liberation Organisation's (PLO) parliament-in-exile, held in the Algerian capital.
The Palestinian Declaration of Independence, read by Arafat, was written by renowned Palestinian poet Mahmoud Darwish.
It had previously been adopted by the PNC, the PLO's legislative body, with 253 votes in favour, 46 against and 10 abstentions.
In April 1989, the PLO Central Council elected Arafat as the first President of the State of Palestine.
The declaration marked a turning point in the history of the Palestinian national liberation movement, as the PLO formally endorsed the two-state solution as a framework for resolving the decades-long conflict.
It also paved the way for widespread Arab, Islamic and international recognition of the State of Palestine.
The Palestinian people's right to self-determination and statehood has been affirmed in several United Nations General Assembly resolutions.
Resolution 3236 recognises these rights as inalienable, including the right to independence and sovereignty.
Resolution 2649 also reaffirms the Palestinian people's right to self-determination, while Resolution 2672 stresses that respecting their inalienable rights is essential to achieving a just and lasting peace in the Middle East.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Flash floods affect roads near i-City, Section 7 in Shah Alam
Article:
SHAH ALAM: More than an hour of continuous heavy rain caused flash floods along roads in the i-City and Section 7 areas, disrupting traffic movement this afternoon.
Posts shared by users on the Threads application showed floodwaters inundating the areas following heavy rain which began about 1pm.
A user, frhn.jefx, posted a video showing a flooded road near i-City, with several vehicles, particularly motorcycles, forced to stop along the stretch.
Another user, jacketpotato.sa, also shared information on conditions along the same route, showing several cars making their way through the floodwaters.
Another user, charlie.kilo.maggi, shared footage of flash flooding at 2.46pm along the exit from the i-City area.
"Had to take a detour via the area behind the factories (around the Pharmaniaga factory) to get out. Hope everyone stays safe," the post said.
Meanwhile, a user, sashidd, posted a video on the same application showing flooding at a car park in Section 7 and advised the public to abandon plans to visit the area to avoid getting stranded.
Earlier, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in nine states and the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur until 5pm today.
In Selangor, the areas expected to be affected are Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Petaling, Kuala Selangor and Hulu Langat.

Title: Melaka focuses efforts on strengthening state economy - Rauf
Article:
MELAKA: The Melaka government will focus on strengthening the state's economy, attracting investments and expediting the implementation of strategic development projects, while also improving the management of public complaints.
Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said all state development programmes would be implemented in an organised manner to ensure that the people benefit from them.
"I do not want the people to wait too long to see the results of state development. A government that has been given a mandate must immediately get to work for the people.
They do not just want to hear promises. They want to see results," he said at a press conference after taking his oath of office for a second term as Melaka chief minister at Seri Negeri.
On the appointment of state executive council members, Rauf declined to specify a date, saying that the possibility of including representatives from Perikatan Nasional (PN) was still under consideration.
In yesterday's 16th Melaka state election, the alliance between
Barisan Nasional (BN) and PN
secured 24 seats in the state legislative assembly, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) won the remaining four seats.

Title: Fahmi: Smart sensor project for elderly to roll out next year
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A pilot project using smart sensors to detect emergencies and alert caregivers is set to be launched early next year to improve the safety of elderly people living alone.
The initiative is a collaboration between the Federal Territories Ministry and the Communications Ministry, through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC).
Razak Mansion has been selected as the pilot location.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said more than 60 per cent of residents at Razak Mansion were senior citizens, prompting the initiative after she visited the residential development a few months ago.
"This is the first collaboration we have undertaken specifically to protect the elderly community," she said at a press conference at Razak Mansion today.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the six-month pilot, involving between 25 and 50 households, would assess the technology's effectiveness, costs and potential for wider implementation.
The initiative uses Internet of Things (IoT)-based smart sensors designed to detect emergencies, such as falls, and trigger early alerts so that assistance can be provided promptly.
The system uses body heat sensors to detect residents' presence and movements without cameras, allowing their safety to be monitored continuously without compromising their privacy, dignity or personal freedom.
Fahmi said the pilot would also determine whether the technology could help save lives and identify challenges before it was extended to other residential areas.
He also gave an assurance that residents' personal data would be protected throughout the project.
"We will prioritise the safety of the personal data of all participants and residents here at Razak Mansion," he said.
Malaysia's population is ageing, with the number of people aged 60 and above rising to 4.1 million, or 12 per cent of the population, in 2025, from 3.9 million (11.6 per cent) in 2024.
The proportion of people aged 65 and above also increased to eight per cent in 2025, from 7.6 per cent a year earlier, placing Malaysia in the United Nations' category of an ageing society.

Title: Pejuang hopes to contest under PN logo in future polls
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Parti Pejuang Tanah Air (Pejuang) hopes to be given the opportunity to contest under the Perikatan Nasional (PN) logo in future elections through seat-sharing negotiations that take into account the strengths of each component party.
Its president, Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir, said the matter was being discussed internally with PN component parties and Barisan Nasional (BN) to reach a mutual understanding on seat allocations.
He said Pejuang's opportunities to contest in the recent Negri Sembilan and Melaka state elections had been limited due to the cooperation between PN and BN, which saw most seats allocated to parties with established electoral records.
"Pejuang initially hoped to contest at least one seat in Negri Sembilan, including the Gemas and Gemencheh state constituencies.
"However, Gemas was eventually contested by a Wawasan candidate, who had earlier taken over the seat from Bersatu, while Gemencheh was allocated to Umno following the cooperation with BN.
"So, that was the situation we had to navigate, and the same happened in Melaka.
"All these were decisions we made amicably during meetings. There were seat negotiations, but ultimately, the decisions reached were accepted by all parties," he said.
He was speaking at a press conference after delivering his policy speech at Pejuang's 2026 Annual General Assembly (PAT) at the Ideal Convention Centre (IDCC) here today.
Mukhriz said the party's sincerity as part of the coalition was also demonstrated through the commitment of its machinery in supporting PN candidates, regardless of which party they represented.
He expressed confidence that the same approach could be maintained in future seat-allocation negotiations, with the strengths of each party, including MIC, Gerakan, Pejuang and Wawasan, taken into consideration.
He said cooperation with BN also deserved attention, as an understanding between the parties could improve the coalition's chances of defeating Pakatan Harapan (PH).
Citing the Melaka state election results, Mukhriz said combining the votes of the respective parties gave PN and BN an advantage over contesting separately.
"Without an understanding between BN and PN in the Melaka state election, I think PH would have won.
"This is clear proof that when we work together and combine our respective strengths, we can overcome our opponents," he said.

Title: Trade war in focus at Asean summit ahead of Trump arrival
Article:
MANILA:  A key regional summit opened Sunday in Manila, with Southeast Asian heads of state grappling with the Middle East crisis and their own regional flashpoints and global leaders finding common ground over US President Donald Trump's trade war.
Trump is scheduled to arrive Tuesday, near the summit's conclusion, a visit that will include a meeting with the leaders of his fellow Quad countries India, Japan and Australia – the first such sit-down of his second term.
But it was the US leader's tariff blizzard that Brazil's newly re-elected President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva had on his mind Sunday in Manila.
"Brazil has learned an extraordinary lesson after the US decided to impose tariffs (on other countries)," he told reporters on the sidelines of the 11-member Asean  summit.
"Instead of weeping or begging the US government ... to have pity on us, we decided to look for other partners for us to sell and for us to buy from," he said, noting his country's trade with regional states Indonesia and Vietnam had jumped 15 and 13 percent, respectively.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney sounded a similar note at the summit a day earlier while touting a new Philippine free-trade deal and Asean trade talks he said had been "substantially concluded."
The two pacts were "part of a strategy of developing a dense web of reliable partners to create more opportunities ... and reducing our relative reliance on the United States," Carney said.
Lula told reporters he had met with Carney on the summit's sidelines, inviting him to make an official visit to Brazil, and that he hoped to double trade with Canada.
Nearly 20,000 police officers have been deployed around Metro Manila for the summit, with progressive groups predicting a turnout of thousands on Tuesday for an anti-Trump march on the summit site.
Much of the uproar targets the US Pax Silica programme – a supply-chain initiative designed to counter China's dominance in semiconductors and rare earths – whose flagship Philippine project, a 1,620-hectare AI manufacturing hub north of Manila, threatens to displace Indigenous families.
US Ambassador to the Philippines Lee Lipton said last week that a widely rumoured November target date for a deal signing timed to Trump's visit was never in the works.
On Sunday, a crowd of about 200 protesters, some carrying signs reading "the Philippines is not for sale" and "Ban Trump!" clashed with police carrying riot shields who blocked an attempted march towards the summit site.
AFP reporters saw at least three of the demonstrators taken away by officers who placed them in a police van.
[[nid:1578377]]
Two issues that have vexed Asean leaders for years – a languishing South China Sea "Code of Conduct" and their relationship with war-torn Myanmar – look like they will be Singapore's problem when the bloc's rotating chair passes to the city-state in 2027.
Myanmar has been excluded from high-level Asean meetings since a 2021 military coup that ousted the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi and triggered an ongoing civil war.
Thailand, which shares a border with Myanmar and is leading the charge for closer relations, last week called for Naypyidaw's foreign minister to be allowed back into meetings.
Philippine foreign secretary Theresa Lazaro told reporters on Saturday there was "no easing" of the approach being taken with Myanmar, which faces an international ruling later this week on whether it committed genocide against its marginalised Muslim Rohingya minority.
Hopes of achieving a so-called Code of Conduct in the disputed South China Sea between Asean states and China during Manila's year in the chair, meanwhile, have also flagged.
A Southeast Asian diplomat involved in summit preparations told AFP he did not expect a code to be signed at the summit.
Lazaro indicated as much on Saturday, saying negotiations were "80 percent" complete.
"If it happens, then it's a small miracle," said Siew Mun Tang, former head of the Asean Studies Centre at Singapore's ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute.
Beijing claims most of the South China Sea despite an international ruling that its assertion has no legal basis, and its coast guard has clashed repeatedly with that of the Philippines.
The row has reared its head at inopportune times over the Philippines' year in Asean's rotating chairmanship, with a July foreign ministers summit opening less than a day after Chinese and Philippine sailors engaged in a clash.
An Asean defence chiefs meeting last month saw Beijing send only an embassy defence attache, blaming "reckless" statements by Philippine politicians.
Manila later rebuked its own public officials over comments about China, stressing the need for a unified voice as the two countries negotiate.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Negri Sembilan constitutional crisis to be resolved soon, says Zahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The constitutional crisis in Negri Sembilan will be resolved as soon as possible, says Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
He said the coalition would do its best to address the people's concerns and ensure the state administration continued to function smoothly.
"We will do what we can, so the people's problems are resolved and the state administration runs smoothly, in line with the Negri Sembilan Constitution," he told reporters after attending the People's Progressive Party (PPP) Deepavali open house here today.
Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has confirmed that he
withdrew an objection letter
sent to Keeper of the Rulers' Seal Tan Sri Syed Danial Syed Ahmad, reaffirming his support for Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan.
A letter dated Nov 10 had earlier circulated on social media, stating that Ismail and 10 state executive councillors, whose appointments had been revoked, had withdrawn an earlier representation submitted to the Conference of Rulers on Sept 17.
In the letter, Ismail said the decision was made in consideration of the Conference of Rulers' Oct 14 statement and the Seremban High Court order dated June 5, which maintained the status quo on Tuanku Muhriz's position as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
In September, Ismail said he had been
pressured into signing
the Instrument of Proclamation on the removal of Tuanku Muhriz.

Title: Govt monitors data centres' impact on power, water
Article:
PETALING JAYA: The government is examining data centre growth and its impact on electricity and water supplies, alongside wider environmental and social concerns.
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said the government was aware of the substantial energy and water requirements needed to support data centre operations.
"This is one of our main areas of focus. We have established a task force known as the Data Centre Task Force (DCTF), co-chaired by the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry and the Ministry of Digital.
"Through this task force, the government is examining in greater detail the application and approval processes for data centre development.
"Based on the data collected, we can identify the number of data centres currently operating in the country, those in the development pipeline, as well as new investments being undertaken," he told reporters after attending the EmpowerHER Digital 2026 programme today.
Also present were Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) chief executive officer Datuk Azman Ismail and Bandar Utama assemblyman Jamaliah Jamaluddin.
Gobind said the task force also brought together relevant stakeholders, including Tenaga Nasional Bhd, water authorities and state governments.
"The task force also assesses the electricity and water supply requirements needed to support the future growth of the data centre industry.
"I believe this is very important. We are working to ensure that the country makes the necessary preparations and exercises close oversight to ensure every approved data centre development is supported by sufficient electricity and water supplies.
"However, we need to look ahead and ensure that electricity and water supplies remain secure, both in the short and long term, without any disruption.
"I take note of the views raised by Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, the Queen of Malaysia, on the impact of data centre development, and will bring the matter back to the DCTF for discussion."
Yesterday, Raja Zarith Sofiah called on the authorities, private sector and public to assess the impact of data centre development on the environment and community well-being.
The Queen said such assessments must take into account
high electricity and water consumption,
the misuse of land and the effects on residents.
Gobind said the EmpowerHER Digital 2026 programme aimed to empower women by raising awareness of how digital platforms could help grow their businesses and simplify dealings with the government.
The initiative was part of efforts by DNB and the ministry to bring digital opportunities to the wider community, he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] BN never planned to extend cooperation with PN for GE16, says Zahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional (BN) has no plans to extend its cooperation with Perikatan Nasional (PN) for the 16th General Election (GE16).
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said, however, that both sides could still sit down for discussions if the time came and circumstances warranted it.
"What we have gone through, particularly in Negri Sembilan and Melaka, is a political understanding.
"We have never planned to go beyond that, but if the time comes and the situation calls for it, we will sit down together," he told reporters after attending the People's Progressive Party's Deepavali open house here today.
Asked whether BN was still pressing for Parliament to be dissolved, Zahid said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had the right and mandate to seek its dissolution.
The BN-PN cooperation secured 24 of the 28 state seats contested in the Melaka election, giving the alliance a two-thirds majority in the state assembly.
In Negri Sembilan, BN won 18 seats while PN secured 7, giving them a combined 25 seats in the 36-seat assembly, above the 24 required for a two-thirds majority.
