Title: Ipoh Festival 2026 brings four weeks of art, music and culture
Article:
IPOH: The inaugural Ipoh Festival 2026 will turn the city into a cultural stage from Nov 27 to Dec 19, featuring performances, art exhibitions, traditional crafts and community activities.
Held under the theme "Turning the City into a Stage", the four-week festival will convert cafés, galleries, heritage buildings and public spaces into venues for artistic experiences.
Rather than concentrating events at a single venue, it will encourage visitors to explore different parts of the city, particularly Ipoh Old Town.
Highlights include musical theatre performances at selected cafés, outdoor film screenings at Ipoh Padang, traditional craft showcases at Tin Alley and exhibitions by local artists.
The Artisan Rhythm Market at Jalan Bandar Timah will bring together artisans and local businesses, while the Wayang & Makan di Padang programme, organised with Greenery Market, offers an outdoor cinema experience.
The festival will feature the Food and Arts Crawl by Ipoh Mali Theatre Society, combining musical theatre with venue visits, alongside a separate music crawl organised by Indiescape.
At 22 Hale Street Heritage Gallery, a festival information centre will serve as a starting point for visitors to discover Ipoh's history, food and heritage.
The visual arts programme includes Rootbound: Origin and Boundless Expression, presented by Senitra Studio Gallery, and Yellow, a contemporary exhibition inspired by Ipoh and Perak by The Ipoh Fine Arts Class and Perak Contemporary Artists.
Other activities include workshops, music and dance performances, documentary screenings and cultural showcases involving local creative groups.
Spread across four weekends, the programme will feature performances by local musicians and cultural groups, including the Perak Society of Performing Arts, Perak Wind Orchestra and Choir, Kinta Valley Wind Orchestra and Kumpulan Selendang Perak.
Organisers said the festival was conceived as a collaborative initiative to unite local artists, cultural organisations and businesses on a common platform.
It is intended to strengthen Ipoh's identity by connecting its heritage with its contemporary creative scene, while giving younger residents an opportunity to rediscover the stories behind familiar places.
The inaugural edition is designed as the first step towards establishing a signature annual event for Ipoh, inspired by established city festivals such as George Town Festival in Penang and Urbanscapes in Kuala Lumpur.
Organisers hope the event will draw more visitors to participating businesses and encourage residents and tourists to spend more time exploring the city.
Ipoh Festival 2026 is supported by the Ipoh City Council and Tourism Perak, with sponsorship from 22 Hale Street Heritage Gallery and Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd.
Admission is free, except for a few activities requiring prior registration.
For programme details and updates, the public can follow @ipohfestival on Instagram, Facebook and TikTok. - BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: GRS MPs to submit memorandum to PAC, seek expanded Pan Borneo probe
Article:
PAPAR, Nov 15 — Seven Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) Members of Parliament will submit a memorandum to the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) next week seeking an expanded scope of investigation into the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway project, including an examination of the basis and implications of the decision to terminate the Project Delivery Partner (PDP) model in 2019.
Papar MP Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali. their spokesman, said the move was important to ensure that the PAC investigation not only focused on the project’s current status and performance, but also examined previous policy decisions allegedly affecting its implementation schedule, contractor appointments and rising construction costs.
Armizan, who is also GRS secretary-general, welcomed the PAC’s decision on October 19 to investigate the management, financial governance and physical implementation of the project following the tabling of the Auditor-General’s Report (AG’s Report) Series 2/2026.
However, he said the scope of the investigation should cover four key factors relating to the termination of the PDP model on September 22, 2019, to comprehensively identify the actual causes of the project’s delays.
“That is our recommendation to the PAC, that the scope of the investigation be expanded to cover the basis and implications of the termination of the PDP model,” he told reporters after officiating at the closing ceremony of the IP SPARK 2026 programme here today.
Elaborating, Armizan said the first factor was the lack of clarity regarding the implications of the PDP termination in the AG’s Report Series 2/2026, although official responses by the Works Ministry in the Dewan Rakyat on August 2, 2022 and October 19, 2026 had cited the termination of the model as one of the causes of project delays.
“So this is not political talk or political issues determined by people, but an official response in the Dewan Rakyat,” said Armizan, who is also Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister.
The second factor, he said, was the need to obtain clarification on the basis of the Federal Government’s decision to terminate the PDP model in 2019 following a recommendation by the Sabah state administration at the time, including whether a comprehensive study had been conducted before the decision was made.
On the third factor, he said uncertainty over the status of the PDP and contractor appointments following the change of government in May 2018 had allegedly caused construction work on the ground to stall for more than a year before existing contractors were reappointed under the conventional implementation method in 2019.
The disruption was also alleged to have contributed to higher project costs, particularly as contractors faced increases in construction material prices due to inflation, as well as the impact of the Covid-19 pandemic.
He said the fourth factor involved the process of reappointing existing contractors and appointing new ones, which was disrupted following the transition from the PDP model to the conventional method, resulting in some Phase 1A packages only undergoing the appointment process in 2021.
“So we hope that not only government agencies but also the contractors will be called to these proceedings to hear about the pressures and issues they faced,” he said.
He stressed that the GRS memorandum was not intended to find fault with any party, but to ensure that policy decisions concerning public infrastructure projects were not influenced by partisan political considerations to the detriment of their smooth implementation. — Bernama

Title: With MIC’s backing, BN vows to field PPP candidates in upcoming general election, says Zahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Barisan Nasional (BN) is committed to fielding candidates from the People’s Progressive Party (PPP) to represent the coalition in the upcoming 16th General Election (GE16).
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said PPP president Datuk Dr Loga Bala Mohan remained steadfast alongside other coalition partners in efforts to revitalise the party as a new component member of BN.
“In my heart, alongside our partners from Umno, MCA and MIC, the PPP is also our partner.
“With the agreement of Tan Sri SA Vigneswaran (MIC president) and Datuk Seri M. Saravanan (MIC deputy president), I am determined that we will field PPP candidates in the upcoming general election,” he said in his speech at the Malaysia PPP Deepavali Open House here today.
On January 18, it was reported that PPP had been officially accepted as a component party of BN.
The Registrar of Societies (RoS), in a letter dated November 25, 2025, confirmed PPP’s status as a component party within the coalition. — Bernama

Title: Parit Yaani crash: Johor govt to bear medical costs, provide monthly aid to orphaned siblings, says exco
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Nov 15 — The Johor government, through the Johor State Islamic Religious Council (MAINJ), will cover the medical costs, including plastic surgery, for the two orphaned siblings who survived an accident along Jalan Yong Peng-Muar, near Parit Yaani, on November 1.
State Islamic Religious Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khalid said the assistance would also include a monthly allowance, as both children were orphaned following the tragedy.
He said the elder sibling, 11-year-old Hasya Fahira Zulkifli, had been readmitted to hospital and was scheduled to undergo plastic surgery on her leg, while her younger brother, Muhammad Adam Mohd Hardi, 8, was now able to walk but still required several follow-up treatments.
“MAINJ’s monthly financial assistance will continue until both siblings receive Survivors’ Pension benefits from the Social Security Organisation (PERKESO), as we understand their father had made contributions.
“The state government will continue to monitor the progress of both siblings… besides MAINJ, we have also been informed that the Social Welfare Department (JKM) is providing assistance,” he told reporters today.
He said this after accompanying Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi to visit Hasya Fahira at a ward at Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital (HSNI), where they also celebrated her 11th birthday today.
Elaborating, Mohd Fared said the state government was also prepared to cover other expenses should the need arise.
“Assistance of this nature is not limited to these two siblings but is extended to all Johoreans in need,” he added.
In the November 1 accident, which occurred at about 12.30pm, the siblings’ parents, Tengku Syafirana Tengku Abdullah, 44, and Mohd Hardi Mohd Husin, 46, were killed after the multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) they were traveling in was crushed by a tar-laden lorry, which had skidded following a tyre blowout.
In the incident, Mohd Hardi sustained serious injuries to his head and both hands, as well as burns to his body, while Tengku Syafirana suffered serious head and internal injuries, as well as burns to her body. — Bernama

Title: Vehicles over 5m barred from Sibu road section beside Dataran Tun Tuanku Bujang until Feb 28 for festive decor
Article:
SIBU, Nov 15 — Vehicles exceeding five metres in height are prohibited from entering a designated road section beside Dataran Tun Tuanku Bujang until Feb 28, 2027 to accommodate Christmas street lighting and festive decorations.
Sibu Municipal Council (SMC) in a statement said the restriction, which took effect on November 14, applies to the road section beside Dataran Tun Tuanku Bujang, behind the WTK Holdings Berhad building.
The council said the temporary measure was necessary to ensure public safety as Christmas decorations and lighting installations would be suspended above the roadway.
SMC advised transport operators, lorry drivers, business operators and members of the public to plan their journeys accordingly and comply with all on-site instructions.
Meanwhile, the council said the Sibu Christmas Celebration 2026, themed ‘Lighting Up Sibu, Celebrating Christmas Together’, aimed to bring the community together, promote cultural harmony and share the joy of the festive season.
“Through the celebration, the council hopes to create a warm, joyful and welcoming festive environment where families, friends, residents and visitors of all ages can gather and enjoy the Christmas spirit,” it said.
SMC added that Christmas symbolised love, peace, hope and the spirit of giving, values that transcended racial, religious and cultural boundaries.
The council said the festive lighting and activities were also expected to enhance Sibu’s appeal, attract visitors and create business opportunities for local traders, food operators and the tourism industry.
SMC thanked the public for their understanding and cooperation in observing the temporary restriction and invited everyone to take part in the Christmas celebration. — The Borneo Post

Title: Senator warns early Parliament dissolution could derail Budget 2027 and force temporary spending, citing 2022 precedent
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 15 — Calls for an early dissolution of the Dewan Rakyat are ill-timed as Budget 2027 has yet to complete the parliamentary approval process, said Senator Datuk Ahmad Ibrahim.
He said dissolving Parliament before the Budget was passed could disrupt the government’s financial planning and delay funding for development projects, infrastructure programmes and other public commitments.
Ahmad said that while the Prime Minister could seek the dissolution of Parliament under the Federal Constitution, subject to the discretion of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, the timing of such a move should be carefully considered.
“My concern is not about whether Parliament can be dissolved, but whether this is the appropriate time to do so,” he said in a statement.
Ahmad, who chairs the Senate Select Committee on National Defence and Security, pointed out that Budget 2027, involving hundreds of billions of ringgit in government expenditure, was still undergoing parliamentary scrutiny.
The Dewan Rakyat is scheduled to complete its committee-stage deliberations on November 26, while the Dewan Negara will begin its deliberations on November 30.
Ahmad said the legislative process should be allowed to run its course, warning that dissolving Parliament before the Supply Bill completes the approval process could result in it lapsing.
“This would require a new government and Parliament to reintroduce and approve the Budget, potentially delaying financial authorisations needed to sustain government operations and implement planned programmes.
“Although temporary expenditure arrangements could be made under constitutional provisions, these would still require further legislative action,” he said.
He cited the October 2022 dissolution of Parliament, which took place just three days after Budget 2023 was tabled.
Following the formation of a new government, Parliament had to approve about RM107.7 billion in temporary operating expenditure in December 2022 to ensure that government operations could continue pending approval of the full Budget.
“Why unnecessarily risk repeating such complications?”
Ahmad said Malaysia was already facing an increasingly uncertain global environment, marked by geopolitical tensions, economic instability, employment concerns, food security issues and the rising cost of living.
“The last thing we need is additional uncertainty surrounding our national financial planning,” he said. — The Borneo Post

Title: Kedah aims to cut operating deficit to 10.59pc with RM1.34b Budget 2027, says MB
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Nov 15 — The Kedah state government today tabled its RM1.34 billion Budget 2027, projecting an operating deficit of RM90 million or 10.59 per cent, for the year.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor said the state government had estimated revenue of RM850 million under the budget, themed ‘The Greater Kedah: Mensejahterakan Rakyat’, while operating expenditure was projected at RM940 million.
He said the revenue target represented an increase of RM12 million from the RM838 million targeted in 2026, with land revenue contributing the largest share at RM551 million, followed by miscellaneous revenue (RM253 million), forestry revenue (RM30 million) and district revenue (RM16 million).
“Of the total operating expenditure allocation, RM81.66 million is set aside for charged expenditure, while RM858.34 million is allocated for supply and services expenditure.
“The 2027 Budget also includes allocations for the State Development Fund, Forest Development Fund and Water Supply Development Fund, with total development expenditure amounting to RM401.28 million,” he said when tabling the Kedah Budget 2027 at the Kedah State Legislative Assembly sitting at Wisma Darul Aman here today.
He said RM245 million of the development allocation was set aside for the State Development Fund, involving 10 implementing departments, while RM12.53 million was allocated for forestry development.
The Water Supply Development Fund received RM143.75 million, comprising RM138.75 million from federal government loans for the implementation of three loan-funded projects and RM5 million from the state government’s allocation.
“The state government also aims to gradually reduce its operating deficit to 10.59 per cent in 2027, from 12.65 per cent in 2025 and 11.81 per cent in 2026.
“This reflects the state government’s commitment to strengthening its fiscal position through expenditure controls, improved management efficiency and optimisation of state revenue sources to ensure long-term financial sustainability,” he said.
The 2027 Budget is the second year of the implementation of the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), continuing the state’s development agenda based on the Kedah Development Plan 2035 and The Greater Kedah 2050, with emphasis on ensuring that economic progress also improves the people’s well-being. — Bernama

Title: BN to skip Sarawak state polls under Umno-PBB understanding, says Zahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Barisan Nasional (BN) will not contest any seats in the 13th Sarawak state election, its chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
The decision is in line with an understanding between Umno and Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB), Ahmad Zahid, who is also Umno president, said.
“BN has no intention of contesting any state seats in Sarawak, as this is the understanding between Umno and PBB in the state,” he told reporters at the People’s Progressive Party (PPP) Deepavali open house here today.
Also present were PPP president Datuk Dr Loga Bala Mohan and MIC deputy president Datuk Seri M. Saravanan.
The Election Commission (EC) has set Dec 12 as polling day, with nomination scheduled for Nov 28
On the possibility of Parliament being dissolved, Ahmad Zahid, who is also Deputy Prime Minister, said the decision rested with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, saying that he (Anwar) has the right and mandate to do so.
On the political crisis in Negeri Sembilan, Ahmad Zahid said efforts would be made to resolve the situation as soon as possible.
He said the necessary steps would be taken to address the problems faced.
“What matters is that the people’s problems in Negeri Sembilan are resolved and that the state administration runs smoothly and in accordance with the Negeri Sembilan Constitution,” he said. — Bernama

Title: ‘Do not be alarmed’: MetMalaysia to conduct tsunami warning siren test in Kudat tomorrow
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 15 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) will conduct a siren test for the Malaysian Tsunami Early Warning System (SAATNM) at the Kudat District Police Headquarters (IPD) tomorrow.
In a post on Facebook, MetMalaysia said the test is scheduled to take place between 9 am and noon.
“Residents in the surrounding areas are advised not to be alarmed by the sound of the sirens, as this is merely a test.
“MetMalaysia will provide updates should there be any changes,” the statement read. — Bernama

Title: Ageing 40-year-old water tank bursts in Kuala Kangsar, affecting 520 consumers; no damage or injuries reported
Article:
IPOH, Nov 15 — The bursting of a 455-cubic-metre water tank at Taman Kuala Kangsar in Kuala Kangsar yesterday was caused by the condition of its structure, which was more than 40 years old.
Perak Infrastructure, Energy, Water and Public Transport Committee chairman Datuk Seri Mohammad Nizar Jamaluddin said the Kuala Kangsar operations centre of the Perak Water Board (LAP) received information about the incident at about 5pm, which affected water supply to approximately 520 consumers in the surrounding areas.
He said LAP had carried out washing and cleaning works on roads around the burst Taman Kuala Kangsar tank, while direct water supply through the main pipeline to the affected areas, namely Taman Kuala Kangsar and Taman Meranti, had also been implemented.
“The removal of all affected tank panels has been carried out, and plans are being made to replace the tank with a new one.
“In addition, LAP is conducting a comprehensive technical assessment of the old tank structure before installation of the new tank begins,” he said in a statement today.
Mohammad Nizar said preliminary investigations at the scene found that the burst tank had caused water to overflow onto surrounding roads, but no reports of casualties or property damage had been received so far.
“An inspection of the house located nearest to the tank also found that it was safe and had sustained no damage,” he said.
Meanwhile, Mohammad Nizar said water supply in the affected areas remained stable and uninterrupted, and the Kuala Kangsar LAP operations centre would continue to monitor the situation to ensure there were no disruptions to water supply and to prevent a recurrence.
Several videos of the tank bursting incident have gone viral on social media since yesterday, causing panic among residents. — Bernama

Title: Selangor flood evacuees fall to 1,399; Perak down to 191
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — The number of flood evacuees at temporary relief centres in Selangor and Perak declined as of 4pm today.
In SELANGOR, 1,399 people from 370 families were still taking shelter at six relief centres in Kuala Selangor, down from 1,493 people from 398 families this morning.
According to the Social Welfare Department’s (JKM) InfoBencana portal, Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Parit Mahang recorded the highest number of evacuees at 420, followed by SK Dato’ Maharaja Lela (391), Sekolah Rendah Agama (SRA) Bukit Kuching (287), Bukit Kuching Tengah Community Hall (119), KAFA Integrasi Hidayah Bukit Cherakah (114) and SRA Batu 8 Ijok (68).
In PERAK, the number of evacuees also fell to 191 people from 58 families, compared with 293 people from 85 families this morning.
All 191 evacuees were housed at the Teluk Intan Municipal Council’s Rest House Hall in Hilir Perak.
The State Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said the SK Khir Johari relief centre in Muallim, which had accommodated 94 people from 25 families, was closed after floodwaters in Kampung Berop receded completely. — Bernama

Title: One hour of rain, roads under water: Flash floods hit Shah Alam’s i-City
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 15 — More than an hour of continuous heavy rain caused flash floods along roads in the i-City and Section 7 areas here, disrupting traffic movement this afternoon.
Posts shared by users on the Threads application showed floodwaters inundating the areas following heavy rain which began at about 1pm.
A user, frhn.jefx, posted a video showing a flooded road near i-City, with several vehicles, particularly motorcycles, forced to stop along the stretch.
Another user, jacketpotato.sa, also shared information on conditions along the same route, showing several cars making their way through the floodwaters.
Another user, charlie.kilo.maggi, shared footage of flash flooding at 2.46pm along the exit from the i-City area.
“Had to take a detour via the area behind the factories (around the Pharmaniaga factory) to get out. Hope everyone stays safe,” the post said.
Meanwhile, a user, sashidd, posted a video on the same application showing flooding at a car park in Section 7 and advised the public to abandon plans to visit the area to avoid getting stranded.
Earlier, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in nine states and the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur until 5pm today.
In Selangor, the areas expected to be affected are Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Petaling, Kuala Selangor and Hulu Langat. — Bernama

Title: Seats, candidates, strategy — Sarawak DAP will decide, says Loke
Article:
KLUANG, Nov 15 — DAP has given full autonomy to the Sarawak DAP leadership to decide how many seats to contest, who to field and its strategy for the upcoming Sarawak state election, party secretary-general Anthony Loke said.
He said that after yesterday’s Melaka state election, the party’s focus has shifted to preparing for the polls in the Land of the Hornbills.
“All decisions concerning the Sarawak state election will be made by Sarawak DAP. The party has indeed granted Sarawak DAP autonomy to make decisions on the number of seats, candidates and strategies,” he told a press conference at the 2026 Johor DAP Convention here today.
He said the central leadership would continue to provide strong support to ensure the smooth running of the party’s machinery in Sarawak.
Asked about the party’s seat projections and the challenges it would face in the state election, Loke said details would be announced by the Sarawak DAP leadership at an appropriate time.
“Of course, some may ask whether it will be a tough election. Definitely, all elections are tough; no election is easy,” he said.
The Election Commission has set Dec 12 as polling day, Nov 28 for nomination and Dec 8 for early voting. — Bernama

Title: From setbacks to comeback? Dzulkefly wants Amanah ready for GE16
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 15 — Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah) must use its defeats in several state elections as a springboard to strengthen the party and prepare its machinery for the 16th General Election (GE16), its vice-president Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said.
He said the entire party leadership and machinery, particularly the youth and young women, must self-reflect, strengthen the organisation and devise more effective strategies for reaching out to the people.
He said the defeats in past elections should serve as a lesson and a catalyst for building new strength, rather than weakening morale or confidence in the party’s struggle.
“We may have lost some battles, but we must make sure we are better prepared to reach the people,... we have lost the battle, but we want to win the war. In the GE16 war to come, we will do our best,” he told reporters after officiating the Wanita Muda Amanah national convention (Warda) here today.
Dzulkefly said Amanah’s struggle should not be centred solely on electoral victory; rather, political victory must serve as a means to build a united, strong and dignified nation-state grounded in the values of human dignity (karamah insaniah).
In his speech, he said the party’s goal is to uphold the dignity of every individual regardless of race, religion, ancestry or social standing, while celebrating diversity in society.
“Victory is not everything; it is the means to an end — a means to a higher and nobler goal. We want to drive a united, strong and dignified nation-state that celebrates diversity,” he said.
Meanwhile, Dzulkefly described the country’s economic performance under the Unity Government led by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim as commendable compared with previous decades, citing positive economic growth, rising foreign investment, low inflation and unemployment, and a strengthening ringgit.
He said these achievements should be leveraged by Amanah to bolster public confidence in the Unity Government, and to ensure that the government’s policies and successes are translated into a political approach close to the pulse of the people.
On GE16, Dzulkefly said there was no need for the general election to be held in the near future, and that it should instead be held in accordance with the parliamentary term.
He said the government need not rush to dissolve Parliament, as the current focus is on sustaining economic growth momentum and strengthening the country’s financial position and industrial sector. — Bernama

Title: Loke says Anwar need not bow to calls for early dissolution of Parliament
Article:
KLUANG, Nov 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim need not bow to calls for an early dissolution of Parliament as long as he continues to command the support of a majority of Members of the Dewan Rakyat, said DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook.
He said the Anwar-led government still had about one year remaining in its term, which should be used to focus on implementing its reform agenda and key national policies.
“As long as the Prime Minister commands the support of a majority in the Dewan Rakyat, there is no reason for him to bow to any pressure,” he said.
He was speaking at a press conference after the 2026 Johor DAP State Annual Convention here today, in response to calls from certain quarters for an early dissolution of Parliament to resolve the current political impasse.
Loke said one of the government’s priorities was to advance planned legislative reforms, including amendments to the Federal Constitution and the enactment of new laws.
He said these efforts were crucial to strengthening administrative governance, improving the country’s financial management and ensuring more effective implementation of the anti-corruption agenda.
“The Prime Minister should use this one-year period to carry out such work and reforms rather than bowing to pressure to dissolve Parliament,” he said.
On the constitutional position, Loke clarified that the power to dissolve Parliament rests with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, who acts on the advice of the Prime Minister in accordance with the Federal Constitution.
He also reaffirmed that Pakatan Harapan (PH) leaders remained united in supporting Anwar’s leadership to ensure political stability in the interests of the people and the nation. — Bernama

Title: Anwar meets Carney in Manila, with Malaysia-Canada energy and digital trade on the table
Article:
MANILA, Nov 15 — Efforts to expand trade and investment cooperation, particularly in the energy, digital economy and technology sectors, were among the key matters discussed during a meeting between Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Canadian counterpart, Mark Carney, here.
Anwar said the meeting, held on the sidelines of the 49th Asean Summit, also touched on bilateral relations as well as regional and international developments.
“I also shared updates on Malaysia’s economic progress and explored potential new areas of collaboration, especially as we approach the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Malaysia and Canada.
“Malaysia and Canada will continue to strengthen their friendship and cooperation for the mutual benefit and prosperity of both nations,” he said in a post on X today.
Anwar is in Manila to lead the Malaysian delegation to the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits, which are being held from November 15 to 17. — Bernama

Title: Ab Rauf’s second-term to-do list: Economy, investments and fewer unanswered complaints
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 15 — The Melaka government will focus on strengthening the state’s economy, attracting investments and expediting the implementation of strategic development projects, while also improving the management of public complaints.
Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said all state development programmes would be implemented in an organised manner to ensure that the people benefit from them.
“I do not want the people to wait too long to see the results of state development. A government that has been given a mandate must immediately get to work for the people. They do not just want to hear promises. They want to see results,” he said.
He was speaking at a press conference after taking his oath of office for a second term as Melaka chief minister at Seri Negeri here today.
On the appointment of state executive council members, Ab Rauf declined to specify a date, saying that the possibility of including representatives from Perikatan Nasional (PN) was still under consideration.
In yesterday’s 16th Melaka State Election, the alliance between Barisan Nasional and PN secured 24 seats in the State Legislative Assembly, while Pakatan Harapan won the remaining four seats. — Bernama

Title: Fresh faces or familiar names? Abang Johari says GPS candidate list coming Nov 25
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 15 — Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) will announce the full list of all 82 candidates who will contest in the 13th Sarawak state election on Nov 25, said its chairman, Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg.
Abang Johari, who is also the president of Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB), hinted at the possibility of changes to the party’s candidate list, aiming to provide an opportunity for a mix of young and experienced leaders.
“Certainly, there may be some changes, with a mix of younger individuals and experienced figures among the candidates we will put forward.
“We will share the details with you on November 25, all 82 candidates so please wait until then,” he said when met by reporters after the PBB Southern Zone Convention here today.
Earlier, while addressing the event, Abang Johari urged PBB members who are not selected as candidates for this state election to continue supporting whoever is chosen.
He said this spirit and culture of mutual support form the foundation of PBB’s success, serves as the anchor party within the GPS coalition.
“Even if you are not chosen as a candidate, the spirit remains, just as others would support us, we must likewise support them. Having PBB representatives is crucial because our party is strong, stable, and possesses sufficient resources to remain self-reliant,” he said.
Earlier, Abang Johari hinted that eight incumbent State Legislative Assembly members from GPS might be retained as candidates involving four PBB representatives namely Fazzrudin Abdul Rahman, Datuk Ibrahim Baki, Datuk Hamzah Brahim, and Datuk Martin Ben.
The other four incumbents are from the Sarawak United Peoples’ Party (SUPP): Datuk Seri Dr. Sim Kui Hian, Datuk Lo Khere Chiang, Wilfred Yap Yau Sin, and Datuk Ding Kuong Hiing.
GPS comprises four component parties namely PBB, SUPP, Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS), and the Progressive Democratic Party (PDP).
The Election Commission (EC) has set November 28 as nomination day, with early voting scheduled for December 8 and polling day for December 12. — Bernama

Title: Stormy evening ahead as MetMalaysia issues warning for multiple states
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected to hit parts of Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak until 8pm today, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia).
In an alert issued at 3.30pm, MetMalaysia said the affected areas in the peninsula include Perlis; Penang; and several districts in Kedah, Perak, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan and Terengganu.
In Kedah, the warning covers Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Kota Setar, Kuala Muda, Yan, Pendang, Pokok Sena, Kulim and Bandar Baharu. In Perak, the districts affected are Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Kinta, Kampar, Perak Tengah, Manjung, Bagan Datuk and Hilir Perak.
The department also forecast similar weather conditions in Hulu Terengganu, as well as Sepang, Kuala Langat and Sabak Bernam in Selangor, and Seremban and Port Dickson in Negeri Sembilan.
In Sarawak, the warning covers Kuching, Sarikei, Kanowit, Sibu, Mukah and Betong.
For Sabah, the affected areas are Tuaran, Kota Kinabalu, Penampang, Putatan, Papar and Ranau on the west coast, as well as Tambunan, Membakut and Keningau in the Interior, and Kinabatangan in Sandakan Division.
MetMalaysia said thunderstorm warnings are issued when there are indications of thunderstorms producing rainfall exceeding 20mm per hour that are imminent or expected to last for more than an hour.

Title: Kedah Sultan gives nod to UUM’s RM15m Kedah Tua Museum plan
Article:
SINTOK, Nov 15 — The Sultan of Kedah, Al Aminul Karim Sultan Sallehuddin Sultan Badlishah, has consented to Universiti Utara Malaysia’s (UUM) proposal to build a Kedah Tua Museum to preserve and promote the state’s historical treasures and heritage.
His Royal Highness said the museum project would require an allocation of RM15 million, covering the construction of a new building, public exhibition areas, digital exhibition spaces, a conservation laboratory, artefact storage, research and management facilities.
He said the museum would showcase the grandeur of the ancient Kedah civilisation for the appreciation of younger generations, including its governance, topography, history and the Sungai Batu civilisation.
“The museum will also house various historical artefacts, including swords, iron ore, iron furnaces and a collection of currency,” he said.
His Royal Highness said this in conjunction with UUM’s 39th Convocation Ceremony here today, where he also conferred degrees on 105 graduates.
He hoped the government would give due attention to the project and consider making it one of the state’s tourism products. He also expressed hope that philanthropists would come forward with contributions to help make the project a reality.
His Royal Highness said Kedah had a long history of civilisation, having emerged as a prosperous kingdom based on trade and the iron industry from the early days of civilisation in the region.
“Iron smelting activities that flourished in the Sungai Batu and Bujang Valley areas not only met local needs but also attracted traders from various regions, making Kedah one of the major economic centres in Southeast Asia,” he said.
Meanwhile, he reminded the graduates that the degrees they received did not merely mark the end of their academic journey, but also the beginning of new duties and responsibilities.
A total of 6,442 graduates will receive their degrees during the convocation, which runs from Nov 15 to 19 at UUM’s Dewan Mu’adzam Shah.
The Royal Education Award was presented to Irfan Umar Mohd Nor Fazly, 24, from Petaling Jaya, Selangor, and Ooi Sze Qin, 24, from Cheras, Selangor, while the Chancellor’s Gold Medal was awarded to Aina Najihah Safaruddin, 24, from Kuala Kangsar, Perak.
Recipients of the Royal Education Award received RM7,500 in cash and a certificate, while the recipient of the Chancellor’s Gold Medal received RM5,000 and a certificate. — Bernama

Title: ‘I’m CM for everyone’, says Ab Rauf as he calls for unity after Melaka polls, declares Nov 16 holiday
Article:
MELAKA, 15 Nov — A day after the 16th Melaka State Election, Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has called on the people of the state to unite as one big family, setting aside any differences in views or political affiliations that may have emerged during the election.
He stressed that he was the Chief Minister for all Melakans, regardless of their political preferences.
“I am not the Chief Minister only for those who voted for me. I am the Chief Minister for all the people of Melaka, regardless of race, religion, background or political inclination,” he told reporters after taking his oath of office as the 13th Melaka Chief Minister, marking his second term, at the Office of the Yang Dipertua Negeri at Seri Negeri today.
He also reminded elected representatives of the trust and responsibility that came with the mandate entrusted to them by the people.
“To my fellow elected representatives who have received this mandate, I wish to remind you never to forget that this position is a trust, not a privilege. I also want the state administration to be more efficient and responsive,” he said.
Meanwhile, Ab Rauf announced that tomorrow, Monday (Nov 16), would be a special public holiday in Melaka.
He said the holiday was declared in conjunction with the victory of Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) in the 16th Melaka State Election.
In the election held yesterday, the BN-PN coalition secured 24 seats in the State Legislative Assembly, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) won four.
Ab Rauf said the special holiday was a gesture of gratitude and appreciation to the people for giving the two coalitions the mandate to continue administering the state.
“It is a token of appreciation to all the people of Melaka who have placed their trust in us and given us the mandate to continue administering the state.
“For that reason, I am pleased to announce Monday, Nov 16, as a special public holiday for the State of Melaka,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar urges Asean to diversify food, medicine supply sources amid global uncertainty
Article:
MANILA, Nov 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called on Asean member states to diversify their sources of food and medicines while strengthening regional production capacity to reduce reliance on external suppliers amid growing global uncertainties.
He said recent global disruptions had exposed the risks of depending on a limited number of suppliers for essential goods, underscoring the need for greater regional cooperation to safeguard supply chains.
In his intervention at the plenary session of the 49th Asean Summit here today, Anwar said member states should increase intra-regional trade in agricultural inputs, including fertilisers, seeds and animal feed, while ensuring the uninterrupted movement of essential supplies across borders during crises.
“Nowhere is this more urgent than in food and medicines, the essentials our people cannot do without.
“Bolstering regional food security must start with fertilisers, seeds and feed, much of which we source from beyond our region.
“Asean must strengthen resilience across this whole chain: trading more of these inputs among ourselves, keeping essential food and agricultural inputs flowing through trusted green lanes in times of crisis, and collectively optimising regional reserves such as the Asean Plus Three Emergency Rice Reserve,” he said.
On medicines, Anwar urged Asean countries to recognise one another’s regulatory approvals, pool their purchasing power and stockpiles, and expand regional manufacturing of essential medicines and vaccines.
He said the Covid-19 pandemic had demonstrated how quickly supply chains could break down during times of crisis.
“We must not be complacent, climate change and environmental degradation make the looming risk of a future pandemic a statistical probability.
“Asean must redouble our efforts on accessibility of medicines by mutual recognition of regulatory approvals, pooling our purchasing power and stockpiles, and building regional manufacturing capacity for essential medicines and vaccines,” he said.
On energy, Anwar said the Asean Power Grid (APG) remained the bloc’s foremost strategic priority.
He urged Asean to accelerate work on the grid, saying national power grids could no longer operate in isolation with regional energy demand projected to quadruple by 2060.
“Accelerating the APG turns individual vulnerabilities into collective strength, unlocking cross-border renewable power sharing and guaranteeing an affordable, secure energy future for our people,” he said.
On the digital economy, Anwar welcomed the signing of the Asean Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA), which he said would help double the region’s digital economy to US$2 trillion by 2030.
“Yet as AI increasingly shapes the global economic and security landscape, its development and governance must not be dictated by the commercial interests of a handful of global technology corporations,” he said.
Anwar urged Asean member states to strengthen their collective technological capabilities, safeguard data sovereignty and establish governance frameworks that uphold transparency and accountability.
The meetings running from Nov 15 to 17 under the Philippines’ chairmanship themed, “Navigating Our Future, Together”. — Bernama

Title: Living alone, but not alone: AI pilot at Razak Mansion aims to spot falls and raise alarms
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Elderly residents living alone at Razak Mansion could soon have an additional layer of protection through a new pilot project using artificial intelligence (AI), radar and thermal sensors to detect falls and unusual inactivity in their homes.
The six-month pilot will involve equipping up to 50 homes with sensor-based technology that can identify when an elderly resident has fallen or shows signs of unusual inactivity, triggering alerts to caregivers and the relevant authorities.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the initiative would explore how technology, particularly the Internet of Things (IoT), could be used to improve the safety and care of older adults as part of wider smart city efforts.
“We often see technology such as the Internet of Things being used for other things, but not necessarily in the context of caring for the elderly in smart cities.
“That is why we are trying to work on this programme, to see whether lives can be saved and what challenges exist before we try to implement it in other places,” he said.
The system will use radar and thermal sensors instead of cameras, allowing residents to be monitored without visual surveillance inside their homes.
When the sensors detect a fall or an absence of movement that triggers an alert, notifications will be transmitted through internet-connected devices to caregivers and security personnel, who can then take the necessary action.
Fahmi said the pilot would run around the clock for six months to assess the technology’s effectiveness, safety and sustainability, including whether its operating costs would make it practical for wider implementation.
“The target here is that we want to know how the technology works and also look at the impact.
“We want to make sure that it is safe, privacy-first and sustainable, because it has to be cost-effective for rollout to other places as well,” he said.
He said the project was still in its design and preparation stages, with procurement of the necessary devices and equipment next.
The pilot is expected to begin early next year once the required processes and procurement have been completed.
Fahmi said the number of participating homes and the project’s eventual expansion would depend on the findings, particularly whether the technology could be adapted to other communities with similar needs.
Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh said Razak Mansion was selected after authorities found that more than 60 per cent of its residents were older adults.
She said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and the Kuala Lumpur office had visited the premises several times to assess how the programme could be implemented.
“We were told that more than 60 per cent of the people here are elderly, so we worked with MCMC on a project to help senior citizens who are living alone.
“This is the first programme of its kind to assist elderly residents, and I hope more people living alone at Razak Mansion will participate,” she said.
Hannah said the government hoped to eventually expand the initiative to other areas, adding that greater participation would help establish the programme’s effectiveness.
She said the press conference was also intended to reassure residents about the initiative, as some might be hesitant to participate because it involved two government agencies.
Beyond the technology pilot, Hannah said the government was also working to improve the daily lives of elderly residents through better facilities and learning opportunities.
She said the Federal Territories Department had allocated funding to Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) for walkway improvements, making it easier for older adults to move around and exercise.
Hannah also said she had allocated RM15,000 for English classes for elderly residents, with efforts underway to secure funding for Bahasa Melayu classes.
She said attendance at the English lessons had been encouraging, reflecting the demand for opportunities among older residents to remain active and continue learning.
“In fact, we are looking to add BM (Bahasa Malaysia) classes as well and we hope more people will participate in this pilot project,” she added.
The initiative is part of broader efforts to make Kuala Lumpur more age-friendly while exploring how technology can help protect vulnerable residents living independently.

Title: After Melaka defeat, Fahmi says Pakatan will examine candidates, youth vote and turnout
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) will examine its candidates’ preparedness, youth voting patterns and lower voter turnout as part of a post-mortem following its disappointing performance in the Melaka state election.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the coalition would hold an initial meeting this week to assess the results and identify areas that need improvement ahead of future elections.
He said one of the issues that needed to be examined was whether candidates were adequately prepared to contest their respective seats and carry out effective campaigns.
“This is an experience that we take as a lesson and reflect on what has happened. The party will do a post-mortem to ascertain the aspects that we need to discuss.
“There are a few things that will be discussed, particularly the readiness of candidates, especially in urban areas,” he said.
Fahmi said the coalition would also look at whether its candidates were sufficiently prepared to campaign and connect with voters in the constituencies they contested.
“Usually in urban areas, the candidates are stronger and more prepared. But for some seats, perhaps the issue was the candidates and their readiness to carry out the campaign,” he said.
He said PH would also study the impact of the youth vote and lower voter turnout compared with that in the previous general election.
“Insya-Allah, this week, Pakatan Harapan will hold a meeting to conduct the initial post-mortem,” he said.
The coalition’s performance in Melaka was a setback, with PH winning only four of the 28 state seats contested, compared with five seats in the previous state election.
Barisan Nasional (BN) secured 21 seats, while Perikatan Nasional (PN) won three, giving the BN-PN alliance a combined 24 seats in the 28-member state assembly.
PH’s four victories were all secured by DAP candidates in Kesidang, Ayer Keroh, Kota Laksamana and Bandar Hilir, while the coalition lost Bukit Katil, previously held by its Melaka chairman Datuk Seri Adly Zahari.
Fahmi said the coalition would need to examine the different factors behind the outcome rather than draw conclusions before completing its assessment.
He also pointed to DAP’s performance as one positive aspect, noting that the party had retained its seats.
“This is the first time since the Sabah election where DAP, a component of Pakatan Harapan, did not lose their seats. So this is one positive development,” he said.
The post-mortem will be part of PH’s efforts to identify weaknesses and make the necessary adjustments to improve its electoral performance moving forward.

Title: Fahmi wants stronger WhatsApp verification after scammers impersonate MCMC officers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil wants WhatsApp to strengthen verification of phone numbers linked to its accounts amid growing concerns over scammers exploiting the messaging platform to deceive the public.
He said the government was looking into the issue following reports of scammers misusing telephone numbers and WhatsApp accounts, including impersonating Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) officers.
“At the moment, WhatsApp does not require verification of the account. But in a few countries, recently at the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), I have heard from many countries that they have raised the issue of misuse of WhatsApp for scam calls.
“So one thing that many countries are doing is to verify the identity and the telephone number that are linked to the WhatsApp account,” he said.
Fahmi said the matter was among several measures being explored to address evolving scam tactics, noting that scammers had adapted their methods after authorities introduced technical measures to block spoofing calls.
“Previously, MCMC implemented a technical change that blocked what is known as spoofing calls, and we have successfully implemented that.
“But the scammers have switched to a different method of scamming. So we can see that additional steps are needed,” he said.
His remarks came after police arrested 61 people suspected of involvement in three scam syndicates, including one believed to have impersonated MCMC officers in telephone scams.
Police said the suspects were detained during raids in Seri Kembangan, Selangor, with two other syndicates allegedly involved in fake part-time job offers targeting victims in Indonesia through WhatsApp.
Fahmi also warned the public against individuals claiming to represent MCMC or the Communications Ministry and threatening to terminate their telephone lines.
He stressed that neither the ministry nor MCMC would contact members of the public to issue orders to shut down their telephone services.
“MCMC will not call to give orders to shut down telephone lines. That is the job of the telecommunications company itself.
“The Communications Ministry is also not involved in such actions,” he said.
Fahmi advised anyone receiving suspicious calls to hang up and lodge a report with the police or MCMC rather than following the caller’s instructions.
He also urged scam victims to contact the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) at 997 immediately.
“If you receive a call to cancel your telephone line and suspect that something is wrong, first put down the call. Second, make a report, either to the police or MCMC. You can also call 997,” he said.
WhatsApp already requires users to verify ownership of a phone number through a registration code sent by SMS or telephone call.
However, Fahmi’s remarks point to the possibility of stronger identity verification for numbers associated with accounts, an issue that has also been raised internationally.

Title: Sultan Nazrin confers Perak state honours on 24 recipients at birthday investiture
Article:
KUALA KANGSAR, Nov 15 — The Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah, today conferred state awards and medals of Perak on 24 recipients at Istana Iskandariah in conjunction with his 70th birthday.
His Royal Highness was accompanied by the Raja Permaisuri of Perak, Tuanku Zara Salim.
Also in attendance were the Raja Muda of Perak, Raja Jaafar Raja Muda Musa, and Raja Di Hilir Perak Raja Iskandar Dzurkarnain Sultan Idris Shah.
Present as well were Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and his wife, Datin Seri Aezer Zubin.
The recipients honoured today are among 218 individuals awarded state honours and medals in conjunction with Sultan Nazrin’s birthday, which was celebrated on Nov 6.
Heading the list of recipients today is Secretary-General of the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability, Datuk Anis Rizana Mohd Zainuddin, who was conferred Darjah Dato’ Seri Paduka Mahkota Perak (SPMP), which carries the title “Datuk Seri”.
Sultan Nazrin also conferred the Darjah Dato’ Seri Panglima Taming Sari (SPTS) upon Chief of Defence Force General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman, which carries the title “Datuk Seri Panglima”.
Next on the list was Accountant General Nasran Omar, who was conferred Darjah Dato’ Paduka Cura Si Manja Kini (DPCM), carrying the title “Datuk”.
His Royal Highness also conferred the Darjah Dato’ Paduka Mahkota Perak (DPMP), which also carries the title “Datuk” upon 13 recipients, including State Housing and Local Government chairperson Sandrea Ng Shy Ching, Director-General of Orang Asli Development Department (JAKOA) Muhammad Akmal Ila Ahmad and Chief Executive Officer of Perak State Agricultural Development Corporation (Perak SADC) Mohd Azhar Mohd Yusof.
The Editor-in-Chief of the Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama), Arul Rajoo Durar Raj, was also awarded the DPMP, which carries the title “Datuk”.
Sultan Nazrin also conferred the Darjah Dato’ Pahlawan Taming Sari (DPTS), which carries the title “Datuk Pahlawan” upon six recipients, including Director of Special Branch, Bukit Aman, Datuk Seri Ibrahim Darus, Commander of Northern Brigade, General Operations Force (GOF), SAC Balveer Singh Mahindar Singh and Perak Deputy Police Chief DCP Mohammad Azlin Sadari.
Earlier, Sultan Nazrin and Tuanku Zara attended the Guard of Honour Ceremony, which commenced with a Royal Salute, followed by the playing of the Perak state anthem and a 21-gun salute fired by the 41st Battery of the Royal Artillery Regiment.
Sultan Nazrin then proceeded to inspect the guard of honour.
The investiture ceremony for the Perak State Awards and Medals is being held in two sessions, with the first today, and the second scheduled for Nov 21. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia on track for third straight year of GDP growth above 5pc, says Amir Hamzah
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 15 — The Malaysian economy is expected to record growth of more than five per cent for the third consecutive year, driven by consistently strong economic performance, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
He said Malaysia’s gross domestic product (GDP) grew by 5.1 per cent and 5.2 per cent in 2024 and 2025, respectively, while this year’s performance is also showing the same momentum.
“Alhamdulillah, the important thing is that our GDP this year, God willing, will exceed five per cent for three consecutive years,” he told reporters at the 2026 Finance Run programme organised by the Ministry of Finance (MoF) in conjunction with National Sports Day here today.
He also shared that the preliminary estimates released by the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) indicated that the country’s economy was expected to grow by 5.3 per cent in the third quarter of 2026.
He said this when asked to comment on the third-quarter GDP performance, which DOSM is scheduled to announce on Nov 18.
The country’s GDP growth for the first nine months of 2026 has so far been reported at 5.5 per cent.
Amir Hamzah said this achievement reflected the government’s efforts through the Madani Economic framework to raise the country’s economic “ceiling,” thereby creating more economic and job opportunities for the people.
Elaborating, he said raising the ceiling was important because further economic development would create better opportunities within the country, including higher-quality jobs.
Amir Hamzah also said that raising the economic ceiling would give the government more room to strengthen the economy’s “floor” to ensure that the benefits of growth could be more widely felt by the people.
In this regard, he said, Budget 2027 emphasises efforts to raise the people’s incomes, including through raising the minimum wage and encouraging government-linked investment companies (GLICs) and government-linked companies (GLCs) to offer fairer wages.
“We can see that many of the initiatives we have undertaken, including the minimum wage policy and efforts involving GLICs and GLCs to raise wages to appropriate levels, are aimed at ensuring that the benefits of economic growth are also passed on to the people,” he said.
At the same time, he said the government understood that not all citizens would directly benefit from economic growth, and therefore targeted assistance such as the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) would continue to be strengthened.
He said that efforts under the Payung Rahmah initiative had also been intensified to help address cost-of-living pressures.
“This is a comprehensive effort by the Madani Government, as we are not only focused on boosting the economy but also want to ensure that the people feel the benefits of the country’s economic prosperity,” he said.
Meanwhile, Amir Hamzah said the Finance Run 2026, organised annually in collaboration with the Ministry of Finance and its agencies, attracted more than 2,000 participants.
He said the programme, which was originally scheduled to take place two weeks ago, had to be postponed due to the haze.
According to him, the programme not only encouraged recreational activities but also strengthened relationships and camaraderie among MoF staff and personnel from its agencies.
This year, the Department of Valuation and Property Services (JPPH) hosted the programme, with agencies taking turns to organise sporting activities to strengthen cooperation and understanding among them. — Bernama

Title: Caught after Threads uproar, man held over alleged RM5 parking fee collection near Maluri MRT
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Police have arrested a local man in his 50s to assist investigations into the alleged illegal collection of parking fees from motorists near the Maluri MRT station, a matter that recently went viral on social media.
Cheras police chief ACP Mohd Rosdi Daud confirmed that the suspect was arrested at about 2pm yesterday.
The issue gained attention after several Threads users claimed that individuals were demanding RM5 from motorists for parking, despite banners at the site stating that parking was free.
In a Threads post yesterday, ParkIt Malaysia said the arrest followed a police report lodged by the company and its efforts to alert the relevant authorities.
The company had earlier clarified that it did not impose parking fees at the location, adding that the Land and Mines Office (PTG) had confirmed that the third party involved was not licensed to operate on the land.
ParkIt Malaysia also pledged to continue cooperating with police to identify those behind the activity and urged the public to share any receipts, company names or QR codes used by the individuals to assist investigations. — Bernama

Title: Ab Rauf is back: Umno man sworn in for a second term as Melaka chief minister
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 15 — Tanjung Bidara assemblyman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh was sworn in as the 13th Melaka chief minister for a second term today.
Ab Rauf, 65, took his oath of office before the Yang Dipertua Negeri of Melaka, Tun Mohd Ali Mohd Rustam, at the Dewan Utama of the Yang Dipertua Negeri’s Office in Jalan Seri Negeri, Ayer Keroh, here, at 12.10pm.
The ceremony was also witnessed by Melaka State Secretary Datuk Salhah Salleh and candidates who won in yesterday’s 16th Melaka State Election.
Also present were Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who is also Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong and MIC deputy president Datuk Seri M. Saravanan.
Earlier, Mohd Ali granted an audience to Ahmad Zahid at Istana Melaka in Bukit Beruang, during which the latter submitted the letter of nomination for the chief minister’s post.
The results of yesterday’s state polls saw Ab Rauf retain the Tanjung Bidara state seat with an 8,615-vote majority, defeating Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate Yunazri Mustamiri in a straight fight.
The BN-Perikatan Nasional (PN) coalition secured a more than two-thirds majority to form the state government, with BN winning 21 seats while PN secured three of the 28 state seats contested.
PH, meanwhile, won four seats. — Bernama

Title: Hard for DAP to swallow, but Anthony Loke’s ministerial exit not a knee-jerk move, says Teo Nie Ching
Article:
KLUANG, Nov 15 — Anthony Loke’s decision to resign as transport minister was not made hastily, but was instead consistent with a stand he has maintained for the past few months, said DAP vice-chairman Teo Nie Ching.
She said while the decision is difficult for the party to accept, Loke’s firm adherence to his principles reflects his commitment to upholding the party’s position on the matter.
Teo, who is also Johor DAP chairman, said Loke made significant contributions to the development of the nation’s transport sector during his tenure leading the ministry, including strengthening the logistics and rail service sectors.
“Seeing a leader who has poured his heart and soul into transforming a ministry step down in order to uphold his principles is truly deeply moving.
“We all know the significant impact of Anthony Loke’s work during his tenure leading the Ministry of Transport,” she said while speaking at the 2026 Johor DAP State Annual Convention held at a restaurant here today.
Earlier, on Tuesday, Loke announced his resignation from the Cabinet effective immediately following a Kuala Lumpur High Court decision that allowed former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest, starting from that day.
Nevertheless, Loke stated that he, along with other DAP members of Parliament, remains supportive of the leadership of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Following this development, Anwar said on Friday that he had yet to make a decision and would hold consultations regarding Loke’s resignation, even though he had already received an official letter from the DAP leader. — Bernama

Title: Rita Rudaini’s eldest brother, a Customs officer, dies after collapsing at Kelana Jaya sports event
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Nov 15 — Ahmad Musyaiful Mokhtar, 51, the eldest brother of actress Rita Rudaini, died of a heart attack after collapsing while participating in a sports activity at the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur Customs Complex in Kelana Jaya early this morning.
Petaling Jaya police chief ACP Shamsudin Mamat confirmed the death, saying it was caused by a heart attack.
“Yes. The cause of death was a heart attack. It is understood that he had a pre-existing heart condition and had previously sought medical treatment for it,” he said in a statement today.
Meanwhile, the Royal Malaysian Customs Department’s Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur office said Ahmad Musyaiful, a senior customs officer in Perlis, collapsed while taking part in a sports activity at the complex.
“He was pronounced dead at 1.45am at the University Malaya Medical Centre after collapsing during a sports activity at the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur Customs Complex in Kelana Jaya, held in preparation for the ongoing Ministry of Finance Sports Festival,” the department said in a statement.
In a separate statement previously reported by the media, Rita described her brother’s death as a profound loss for her and the family.
“The loss of a loved one is, without a doubt, a massive blow to me and my whole family. There are no words to describe how I felt upon receiving this tragic news from his child early this morning,” she said.
Rita also appealed to the public to pray for the deceased, asking that his soul be granted divine mercy, his sins forgiven and that he be placed among the faithful and righteous.
His remains are expected to be transported to his hometown in Kangar, Perlis, for burial. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: ACP stands for Assistant Commissioner of Police.
